subject: HCI 2
title: HCI 2 Prelims — Handheld, Touch, Auditory, Visual, QR Codes & Itertools (50 Items)

questions.text: A handheld device is defined as a computer or digital engine small enough to be operated completely within the palm of:
questions.hint: Core anatomical definition of handheld devices.

questions.text: Which wearable category includes garments with built-in biometric circuitry that can adjust based on ambient temperature?
questions.hint: Also called tech textiles.

questions.text: Which touchscreen technology can be activated by virtually any input object (finger, stylus, gloved hand, pen)?
questions.hint: It works by pressure forcing two layers into contact.

questions.text: Which interaction technique improves target selection for motor-impaired users by letting them drag across a target?
questions.hint: Especially useful in high-density interfaces.

questions.text: Projected Capacitive (P-Cap) touchscreens are particularly susceptible to which type of interference?
questions.hint: Their 3D electrostatic field can be disrupted.

questions.text: Which auditory interface type is a direct translation of a data waveform into the audible domain?
questions.hint: Works best with large datasets that have periodic features (e.g., seismic data).

questions.text: The term "Earcon" is a pun on which visual concept?
questions.hint: Coined by D.A. Sumikawa in 1985.

questions.text: A Geiger counter’s click rate indicating radiation level is an example of:
questions.hint: Non-speech audio used to convey information or perceptualize data.

questions.text: In the auditory interface processing loop, which stage converts data into sound waves/signals?
questions.hint: Stage D is the physical speaker; Stage C does the rendering.

questions.text: QR Codes were invented in 1994 by Denso Wave primarily for:
questions.hint: Denso Wave is a Toyota subsidiary.

questions.text: Which QR error-correction level can recover from up to 30% damage and is ideal when logos are embedded?
Which itertools function produces ordered arrangements where order matters?
questions.hint: 4! = 24 different finish orders for 4 runners.

questions.text: How many permutations does a set of 4 unique items have?
Which statement correctly distinguishes sensation from perception?
options: Sensation is subjective; perception is identical for everyone
Sensation is the physical process (same for all); perception is mental and subjective
Both are purely physiological and identical across people
Perception happens in the eye; sensation happens in the brain
questions.hint: Sensation = camera sensor; Perception = photo editor.

questions.text: Which UI design principle states that interactive components must stand out sharply from their background?
questions.hint: Helps guide visual attention and reduces search time.

questions.text: In the grouper() recipe, when the final group is shorter than n, what is used to pad it?
questions.hint: zip_longest pads shorter iterables with fillvalue.

questions.text: The grouper() recipe works by creating n references to the SAME iterator. What is the key benefit?
options: Allows parallel processing of multiple independent iterators
Each reference consumes the next element, forming non-overlapping chunks
Creates independent data copies for each chunk
questions.hint: No element is ever repeated across chunks.

questions.text: Which touchscreen type provides the highest image clarity because it adds NO overlay layer on the display?
questions.hint: IR uses beams around the frame; nothing sits on the glass.

questions.text: When decoding a QR code with OpenCV, which method returns the decoded data, corner points, AND the straightened QR image?
questions.hint: Returns a 3-tuple: (data, points, straightened image).

questions.text: A Voicemail System’s functionality extends beyond storing messages. Which statement is accurate?
options: It can only play back recorded messages
It can deliver voice information AND process transactions
It requires a smartphone app to function
It converts speech to text automatically
questions.hint: Works over ordinary telephone lines for individuals, organizations, products, and services.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of Wigdor & Wixon’s (2011) design considerations for touch interfaces?
questions.hint: The fourth principle is Size Factor (ergonomics).

questions.text: Which interaction technique is the only one that eliminates the strict requirement for predefined target spaces?
questions.hint: Actions are triggered by motion paths anywhere on the surface.

questions.text: In which year were both the Apple iPhone and Microsoft Surface launched, marking the mainstream touch breakthrough?
questions.hint: Often called the mainstream milestone for modern smartphones and surface computing.

questions.text: Personal Digital Assistants (PDAs) were largely displaced by:
questions.hint: Smartphones absorbed the calendar, contacts, and productivity functions of PDAs.

questions.text: What does the acronym QR stand for?
questions.hint: Designed for fast scanning from any direction.

questions.text: The three bold corner squares that tell a scanner the orientation of a QR code are called:
questions.hint: They act like corner flags on a map.

questions.text: The outer white safety margin of a QR code (minimum 4 modules wide) is called the:
questions.hint: Helps scanners locate and isolate the code.

questions.text: What is the default error-correction level used by Python’s qrcode library?
questions.hint: Corrects up to 15% of errors.

questions.text: Surface Capacitive touchscreens can be activated by:
options: Only human skin (or a specialized capacitive stylus)
Bare finger or thin surgical glove only
questions.hint: They react to the static electrical capacity of the human body.

questions.text: Infrared (IR) touchscreens will NOT activate with which of the following?
options: A hard plastic pen or credit card
questions.hint: Hard items may not interrupt the light beams reliably.

questions.text: In the visual pathway, which stage transforms perceived information into meaningful action (memory, reasoning, decision-making)?
questions.hint: Sensation → Perception → Cognition.

questions.text: The pupil of the eye is analogous to which camera component?
questions.hint: It controls how much light enters.

questions.text: Which auditory type is best described as a brief, distinctive synthesized sound that represents a specific event?
questions.hint: Examples: OS error beep, NBC three-tone chime.

questions.text: Which itertools function is used inside the classic grouper() recipe to pair elements and pad shorter groups?
questions.hint: It pads with fillvalue when one iterable runs out.

questions.text: itertools.permutations() is memory-efficient because it uses:
options: Eager evaluation (builds the full list at once)
Lazy evaluation (generates values only when asked)
questions.hint: Like a vending machine — items appear only when requested.

questions.text: Which of the following is classified as a wearable archetype?
questions.hint: Worn on the body; controlled by integrated electronics.

questions.text: Which touchscreen technology supports full multi-touch and can still work with thin surgical or cotton gloves?
questions.hint: Widely used in modern smartphones.

questions.text: In a QR code, information is carried primarily by:
options: The thickness of the quiet zone
The size of the finder patterns
questions.hint: Position, not color, encodes the data.

questions.text: Why are auditory interfaces useful?
options: They reduce visual overload and support multitasking when sight is limited
They only work for users with visual impairments
They require no training to interpret
questions.hint: Useful while driving or when visual attention is elsewhere.

questions.text: Abrupt changes in screen brightness can cause:
questions.hint: Consistent luminance is one of the UI design principles.

questions.text: The three bold corner squares in every QR code that tell the scanner its orientation are called:
questions.hint: Also accept "Finder Patterns" or "Position detection patterns".

questions.text: The auditory display type that interprets a raw data sequence directly as an audio waveform is:
questions.hint: Direct waveform-to-sound translation.

questions.text: The Wigdor & Wixon (2011) principle stating the interface should feel like a natural extension of the user’s body is called:
questions.hint: One of the four core design considerations.

questions.text: The default error-correction level used by the Python qrcode library (corrects up to 15%) is:
questions.hint: Also accept "Level M" or "M".

questions.text: The mental process that transforms perceived information into meaningful action (memory, reasoning, decision-making) is called:
questions.hint: Sensation → Perception → Cognition.

questions.text: The itertools function used inside grouper() that pairs elements from multiple iterators and pads shorter ones is:
questions.hint: Full name: itertools.zip_longest().

questions.text: The year the Apple iPhone and Microsoft Surface were simultaneously launched:
questions.hint: Mainstream milestone for modern touch interfaces.

questions.text: The outer white safety margin of a QR code (minimum 4 modules wide) is called the:
questions.hint: Also accept "Quiet Zone".

questions.text: List the four types of Auditory Interfaces covered in the module (any order):
questions.hint: Accept any order; minor spelling variations OK.

questions.text: The Python class from OpenCV used to create a QR code detector object is:
questions.hint: Instantiate then call .detectAndDecode().
